text:
To: Finance Staff
From: Arvid Nilsson, Financial Controller
Subject: Year-end closing procedures

The financial year will close on 31 December, and the following procedures apply to all departments. All invoices received by 15 December must be approved and entered into the system by 22 December. [1] Invoices that arrive after this date will be recorded as accruals, which will be reversed in January once the actual amounts are confirmed.

Departments are asked to [2] their outstanding commitments by 18 December, so that the accruals can be estimated with reasonable accuracy. [3] a department fails to do so, the controller's office will make its own estimate, which may differ significantly from the final figure. The external auditors will arrive on 12 January, and they will expect all supporting documents to be [4] by that date.

choices: This deadline allows time for queries to be resolved before the ledgers are locked at the close of business on 29 December.
This deadline allows time for ledgers to be resolved before the queries are locked at the close of business on 29 December.
This deadline allowed time for queries to be resolved before the ledgers were locked at the close of business on 29 December.
This deadline prevents time for queries to be resolved before the ledgers are opened at the start of business on 29 December.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says invoices that arrive after this date are accrued, so the previous one must explain the purpose of the deadline; only the first does.
Departments must 'confirm' their commitments, meaning verify them; the others do not fit.
'Where a department fails to do so' introduces the specific case in which the controller makes an estimate; 'whereas' contrasts, and 'wherein' and 'whereby' do not fit.
'To be available by that date' needs the adjective.
